title: DOJ Opens Criminal Probe into E. Jean Carroll for Alleged Perjury in Trump Civil Suits
detail: The Justice Department under Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche launched a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll on May 28, 2026, focusing on whether Carroll committed perjury during testimony in her civil lawsuits against Trump. Juries awarded Carroll approximately $88 million in damages across two civil trials; Trump is appealing both verdicts. The probe represents an escalation of the administration's use of the DOJ to scrutinize Trump legal adversaries — following the pardoning of Jan. 6 defendants, the firing of federal prosecutors who pursued cases against Trump associates, and the reversal of investigations into Trump allies. Carroll's legal team called the investigation 'politically motivated harassment designed to punish and silence Trump's accusers.' Critics across the legal community warned the probe sets a dangerous precedent of weaponizing criminal justice against civil litigants who prevailed in court. The investigation is one of the most prominent DOJ actions targeting a Trump accuser since his return to office.

media.caption: DOJ opens criminal probe into E. Jean Carroll for alleged perjury in civil suits against Trump

title: Iran Ceasefire Under Maximum Strain: Kuwait Intercepts Ballistic Missile; IRGC Claims US Air Base Strike; Trump Threatens Oman
detail: The fragile US-Iran ceasefire (in effect since April 8, 2026) came under maximum pressure on Day 89 of the conflict. Kuwait's air defenses intercepted a ballistic missile launched toward Kuwaiti territory — an incident CENTCOM characterized as 'an egregious ceasefire violation.' Iran's IRGC simultaneously announced it had struck an unspecified US air base in the Persian Gulf region, framing the attack as retaliation for US 'self-defense' strikes conducted near Bandar Abbas Airport on May 25-26. In a dramatic escalation of rhetoric, Trump threatened Oman — previously viewed as a neutral diplomatic venue for US-Iran back-channel communications — warning that Oman would 'behave or we'll have to blow them up' after reports of an Oman-Iran joint plan to levy transit tolls on ships using the Strait of Hormuz. Trump simultaneously insisted he would 'not be rushed' into an Iran deal and dismissed Iranian state media claims of a near-imminent agreement. Brent crude remained volatile in a $100-104/bbl range. The ceasefire technically holds through Day 89 but diplomats on both sides warn a single miscalculation could restart active hostilities. The Strait of Hormuz remains partially blocked by the US naval blockade with approximately 41 tankers (69M barrels of oil) still unable to pass.

media.caption: Iran ceasefire under maximum strain: Kuwait intercepts ballistic missile; Trump threatens Oman over Strait tolls

title: Republicans Lock In ~10-Seat Structural Redistricting Advantage for 2026 Midterms
detail: CNN reported on May 28, 2026 that Republicans are finishing the 2026 congressional redistricting cycle approximately 10 House seats ahead of Democrats — a structural advantage that makes it significantly harder for Democrats to retake the House majority even amid Trump's historically low approval ratings of 31-37%. The Republican advantage stems from gerrymandering in states where Republicans control both the governor's office and legislature, as well as favorable court rulings in Texas, Georgia, and Florida that allowed heavily partisan maps to stand. Democrats currently lead the generic congressional ballot by +8 points in polling, but the redistricting structural disadvantage means that lead may not translate to a House majority — analysts estimate Democrats would need a 10+ point generic ballot advantage to overcome the map disadvantage and flip sufficient seats. Trump MAGA primary victories (Ed Gallrein over Thomas Massie in KY-04; Julia Letlow over Bill Cassidy in Louisiana) continue to consolidate the Republican coalition behind Trump, further cementing his control over House Republicans heading into the midterms. The report underscores the challenge Democrats face in converting Trump's record-low approval numbers into congressional majorities in 2026.

media.caption: Republicans finish 2026 redistricting cycle ~10 seats ahead of Democrats, creating structural House midterm advantage

title: Federal Judge Declines to Block Trump's Mail-In Voting Executive Order
detail: A US federal judge declined on May 28, 2026 to block Trump's executive order targeting mail-in voting, allowing the order to remain in effect while legal challenges proceed. The order, which critics argue restricts voting access, has faced multiple lawsuits from voting rights groups and Democratic-led states. The ruling is a significant near-term victory for the Trump administration's election integrity agenda and comes amid broader efforts to reshape voting procedures ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. Opponents vowed to continue challenging the order in federal courts, arguing it violates federal voting rights statutes and places unconstitutional burdens on voters.

title: FBI Arrests Senior CIA Official David Rush with $40M+ in Gold Bars, $2M Cash, Luxury Watches
detail: The FBI arrested a senior CIA official identified as David Rush on May 28, 2026, after a search of his Virginia home discovered more than 400 gold bars worth over $40 million, dozens of luxury watches, and approximately $2 million in cash. Rush faces federal charges of criminal theft of government money. The case raises significant questions about oversight at the CIA and how a senior official could accumulate such wealth without detection. Authorities have not yet disclosed how long the alleged theft took place or how the assets were accumulated. The Trump administration faces pressure to explain how CIA internal oversight systems failed to detect the alleged misconduct. The arrest comes amid broader scrutiny of intelligence agencies under the Trump administration following the firing of numerous CIA and intelligence community officials.

media.caption: FBI arrests senior CIA official David Rush with over $40M in gold bars and $2M cash at his Virginia home
